submission.justification: Module-D1 gives the most light (49.5 PE/MeV at 30% coverage) but fails the hard thermal-cycling requirement: 30% of modules failed, against a 5% limit, because the light-guide bonding cracks. Modules can't be replaced once the cryostat is filled, so D1 is ruled out. Of the two designs that pass, Module-D3 collects more light: 38.7 vs 25.6 PE/MeV for D2 at 30% coverage. Light collection rises with coverage, and there are enough feedthroughs for 30%, so I chose the maximum allowed coverage of 30%. Caveat: D3's 2% failure rate comes from a batch of 40 modules, which is about 1 failure. At 95% confidence the upper limit is about 12%, so the test does not yet prove D3 is below 5%. I recommend testing a larger batch before the Q3 design freeze. D2 (0.5% failures) is the fallback if D3 fails that test.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible light collection (PE/MeV)
requirements.evidence: Geant4 at 30% coverage: D1 49.5, D3 38.7, D2 25.6 PE/MeV. D3 at 30% gives the most light among the designs that pass thermal cycling. D1 is excluded by the hard constraint.

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three designs in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Module-D3 (wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: At most 5% of modules may fail after 20 thermal cycles (300 K to 87 K)
requirements.evidence: thermal_cycling_tests.md reports a 2% failure rate for D3 (batch of 40). Caveat: with this sample size the 95% upper limit is about 12%, so a larger qualification batch is recommended. D1 failed at 30%.
30% chosen. Feedthroughs support up to 30% (meeting notes 2026-01-20).
